capabilities: Full .NET API surface with IL2CPP or Mono backend
Native plugin support via DllImport (P/Invoke)
DirectX 12 ray tracing support via HDRP
Steam, Epic, and GOG SDK integration
Multi-monitor and arbitrary resolution support
limitations: Anti-cheat integration requires platform-specific SDKs
Windows Defender may flag IL2CPP builds during development
DirectX 12 backend may have driver-specific issues on older GPUs
recommendations: Use IL2CPP for release builds - Mono is fine for faster iteration
Set target architecture to x86_64 unless 32-bit support is required
Enable incremental GC to reduce frame hitches
Use Burst compiler for math-heavy code paths
Test with both DX11 and DX12 - some players force a specific API

capabilities: Universal Binary support for Intel and Apple Silicon
Metal API with compute shader support
Retina display support via Screen.dpi
App Sandbox and Hardened Runtime for notarization
Steam and Mac App Store distribution
limitations: No Vulkan or OpenGL support since macOS Mojave deprecation
Metal does not support geometry shaders
Code signing and notarization required for distribution
Less reliable GPU profiling tools compared to Windows
recommendations: Build as Universal Binary (ARM64 + x86_64) for full Mac coverage
Use IL2CPP - Mono AOT has limitations on Apple Silicon
Test on both Intel and Apple Silicon hardware
Enable Metal validation layer during development for shader debugging
Handle Application.targetFrameRate carefully - macOS VSync behavior differs

capabilities: Vulkan support with compute shaders
Steam Deck compatibility via Proton or native build
Headless server builds for dedicated game servers
X11 and Wayland display server support
Native plugin support via shared libraries (.so)
limitations: Wide variety of distros and driver versions to test against
Audio backend varies - PulseAudio, PipeWire, or ALSA
Gamepad support depends on kernel and driver availability
Smaller player base makes QA coverage harder
recommendations: Target Vulkan as primary API with OpenGL Core fallback
Test on SteamOS / Steam Deck for the largest Linux gaming audience
Use Headless mode for dedicated server builds to avoid GPU dependency
Bundle required shared libraries or document dependencies clearly
Test with both X11 and Wayland window managers

capabilities: Vulkan support on Android 7.0+ devices
ARCore integration for augmented reality
Adaptive performance API (Samsung and partners)
Google Play Asset Delivery for large games
Split APKs (AAB) and runtime asset downloading
limitations: Extreme device fragmentation - thousands of GPU and SoC combinations
Thermal throttling reduces sustained performance on mobile chips
Vulkan driver quality varies significantly across vendors
64-bit requirement (arm64-v8a) for Google Play since 2019
Background app lifecycle can kill your app without warning
recommendations: Set minimum API level to 24 (Android 7.0) for Vulkan support
Use IL2CPP exclusively - Mono is not supported for arm64
Profile on low-end devices early - Galaxy A series, not just flagships
Use Addressables to keep initial APK size under store limits
Implement Application.lowMemory callback to release cached assets

capabilities: Metal API with GPU-driven rendering support
ARKit integration for augmented reality
Haptic feedback via Core Haptics
On-demand resources for asset streaming
Game Center and StoreKit integration
limitations: IL2CPP only - no JIT compilation allowed by App Store policy
No dynamic code generation (Reflection.Emit, runtime assembly loading)
Metal does not support geometry shaders or tessellation on all devices
Strict App Store review - no hot-patching code at runtime
Xcode required for building and signing
recommendations: Set minimum iOS version to 15.0 for broadest modern device coverage
Use Asset Bundles or Addressables for on-demand content
Enable Metal API Validation in Xcode during development
Minimize managed allocations to avoid GC spikes on older devices
Use On-Demand Resources (ODR) for optional content to reduce download size

capabilities: Runs in any modern browser without plugins
WebAssembly (WASM) compilation for near-native performance
IndexedDB for persistent local storage
JavaScript interop via .jslib plugins
Progressive loading with streaming assets
limitations: No threading - System.Threading and C# async/await are limited
No sockets - use WebSocket or HTTP via UnityWebRequest
Memory is limited by browser tab allocation (typically 2-4 GB)
No file system access - must use IndexedDB or server-side storage
Audio autoplay blocked by browser policy until user interaction
recommendations: Keep build size small - compress with Brotli, strip unused code
Use Addressables with remote asset hosting for large projects
Avoid Instantiate/Destroy loops - use object pooling aggressively
Call WebGLInput.captureAllKeyboardInput(false) if embedding in a page with other HTML
Test in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari - WebGL behavior varies across browsers

capabilities: DualSense haptic feedback and adaptive trigger support
SSD-based asset streaming with near-instant load times
Ray tracing support via hardware RT units
PSN integration for trophies, matchmaking, and commerce
Activity cards and Game Help integration
limitations: Requires PlayStation Partners registration and NDA
DevKit hardware required for testing and profiling
Platform-specific APIs available only under NDA documentation
Certification requirements are strict and time-consuming
Unity PS5 module requires separate license
recommendations: Use platform scripting defines (#if UNITY_PS5) to isolate platform code
Leverage Addressables for SSD streaming - avoid blocking loads
Integrate DualSense features early - they are a TRC expectation
Profile with PlayStation-specific tools (Razor, PIX equivalent)
Plan for certification requirements from the start of production

capabilities: DirectX 12 Ultimate with ray tracing and mesh shaders
Xbox Game Pass and Xbox Live integration
Smart Delivery for cross-generation support
Quick Resume and suspend/resume lifecycle
GDK (Game Development Kit) integration
limitations: Requires ID@Xbox or Microsoft publisher agreement
DevKit hardware required for testing
GDK integration requires specific Unity version support
Certification (XR) requirements are extensive
Two hardware targets (Series X and S) need separate performance profiles
recommendations: Use UNITY_GAMECORE define for shared Xbox code across generations
Target 4K/60fps on Series X and 1080p/60fps on Series S
Implement Quick Resume support - handle suspend/resume lifecycle properly
Use PIX for Xbox for GPU profiling and capture analysis
Plan scalable quality settings to cover both Series X and S from the start

capabilities: Handheld and docked mode detection and resolution switching
Touch screen input in handheld mode
Joy-Con motion controls and HD Rumble
Local wireless multiplayer (LDN)
Nintendo Account and eShop integration
limitations: Tegra X1 GPU is significantly weaker than other current-gen consoles
4 GB RAM total (approximately 3 GB available to games)
CPU is ARM Cortex-A57 - lower single-thread performance than desktop
Must maintain 30fps minimum in both handheld and docked modes
Requires Nintendo Developer Portal registration and DevKit
recommendations: Target 720p handheld / 1080p docked with dynamic resolution scaling
Use aggressive LOD, texture streaming, and occlusion culling
Minimize shader variants - compile times are long on Switch
Pool all allocations - GC pauses are more noticeable at 30fps
Test thermals in handheld mode during extended play sessions
